subtitulo: The three rungs that move you from a fussy opinion to a kitchen that has been told — and the card that does it without your accent
cena: Half nine, a taberna off the square, you have already said your line, and the waitress is smiling and telling you that a tiny bit never hurt anybody.

clique.desconto: Nobody gave you those four questions. You built them out of one word you already own.
clique.piso: You will hand a Spanish kitchen something it can act on. Most people who spend a fortnight here order and hope.

frasePiso: You will hand a Spanish kitchen something it can act on. Most people who spend a fortnight here order and hope.
permissao: You never explain why, and you never apologise for asking. Olive oil is not a battle worth having and garlic is not either, unless it genuinely hurts you. Ask once, at the point of ordering, and then eat your dinner.
espelho: Apologising before you ask is the bit that reads as odd there. You are handing the kitchen information, and information is not a complaint.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You say you are allergic and the waitress smiles and says «un poquito no pasa nada, ¿no?» — a tiny bit is fine, isn't it.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: She thinks I am inventing it. If I push back now I am the difficult foreigner at table nine.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: A first, softly said sentence lands on the same shelf as «I don't really like coriander», because that shelf is full — a busy dining room gets a hundred preferences a week. She is checking which shelf you belong on, not arguing with you.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Say «no», then the five words, with a straight face and your eyes up. Then put the card on the table.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The question stops being about your Spanish and the kitchen gets told for real — and you eat the rest of the fortnight without doing arithmetic over every plate.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not at a counter three deep at midnight. There nobody is having a conversation with anybody: you take the card out first and skip the sentences.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You order the green beans and they arrive with small cubes of ham through them, and nobody mentioned it.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: They served meat to somebody who asked for vegetables. Either they were careless or they were not listening.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: In a kitchen that reaches for cured pork the way yours reaches for a stock cube, ham is seasoning. Seasoning does not get read out with the dish, at home or there.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask what the dish carries before you order it, not after it lands. One question, at the board.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop avoiding the whole vegetable half of the menu and start ordering off it on purpose.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not where the menu is a laminated photo card in four languages — there the vegetables come from a bag and the answer is genuinely no.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Anywhere in Spain serving food that did not come out of a sealed packet has to hold allergen information for every dish — restaurant, bar, bakery or market stall.

steps.pt: Warm-up first: the punch. One syllable per word takes it, and only one. Os-pee-TAL. The punch is at the end.

steps.promptPt: Last night's plate had one thing in it you have hated since you were nine, and a kitchen can leave that out. Ask them to. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-dheh ah-THEHR seen theh-BOH-yah
steps.pt: made without it
Good news first. This is the one conversation in Spain where the law, the kitchen and the waiter are all on your side.
Half nine, a taberna off the square. You have said your line. The waitress is smiling at you.

steps.es: Vale, un poquito no pasa nada, ¿no?
steps.pinyin: BAH-leh, oon poh-KEE-toh noh PAH-sah NAH-dhah, noh
steps.pt: 👂 'A tiny bit's fine though, isn't it?' — the sentence this whole part exists for.
steps.tts: Vale, un poquito no pasa nada, ¿no?

steps.pt: That is not rudeness. A dining room hears a hundred opinions a week, and yours has just landed on the pile.
So the work is not vocabulary. It is moving what you said from opinion to medical fact, in three short steps.
Rung one is the frame that carries this whole part, and it is two words. Soy — I am. Then the label.
The label is the part that moves, and at a table the list is short and closed. Four, and that is the lot.

steps.es: Soy alérgico a los frutos secos.
steps.pinyin: soy ah-LEHR-khee-koh ah lohs FROO-tohs SEH-kohs
steps.pt: I'm allergic to nuts. (a man speaking — the -o ending)

steps.pinyin: soy ah-LEHR-khee-kah al mah-REES-koh
steps.pt: I'm allergic to shellfish. (a woman speaking — the -a ending)
You never pick that ending. The app set it when you signed up and it stays set. One less thing to get wrong.
Listen to the middle of the word, though. Alér-GI-co. That G is a Scottish loch, not an English J.

steps.promptPt: A bar in Madrid. There is a bowl of almonds by the beer taps and the tapa coming your way has been sitting beside it. Say what you are, and to what. Speak now.
steps.es: Soy alérgico a los frutos secos.
steps.pinyin: soy ah-LEHR-khee-koh ah lohs FROO-tohs SEH-kohs
steps.pt: the whole nut family

steps.promptPt: Different coast, different day. Everything that comes out of this kitchen has been in a pan with prawns at some point. Tell her before you sit down. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: soy ah-LEHR-khee-kah al mah-REES-koh
steps.pt: crab, prawns, mussels, the lot
Two more labels, and both land harder in a Spanish kitchen than the English word you would reach for.

steps.es: Soy celíaco. Sin gluten, por favor.
steps.pinyin: soy theh-LEE-ah-koh · seen GLOO-ten, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: I'm coeliac. Gluten-free, please.
Celíaco names a condition, not a diet, and every kitchen knows it. Note the middle: theh-LEE-ah-koh.

steps.promptPt: A bakery counter at nine in the morning, and the woman is already holding the bag open. One word puts you on the right shelf. Say it, then say what you need. Speak now.
steps.es: Soy celíaco. Sin gluten, por favor.
steps.pinyin: soy theh-LEE-ah-koh · seen GLOO-ten, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: the condition, then the request

steps.es: Soy vegetariana: no como carne ni pescado.
steps.pinyin: soy beh-kheh-tah-RYAH-nah · noh KOH-moh KAR-neh nee pehs-KAH-dhoh
steps.pt: I'm vegetarian: I don't eat meat or fish.
Do not drop the last two words. Say only «no como carne» and tuna arrives, and nothing has gone wrong.

steps.promptPt: The waiter is about to point you at the tuna salad as the safe one. Head him off before he does — and say the whole thing, both halves. Speak now.
steps.es: Soy vegetariana: no como carne ni pescado.
steps.pinyin: soy beh-kheh-tah-RYAH-nah · noh KOH-moh KAR-neh nee pehs-KAH-dhoh
steps.pt: and the fish too

steps.pinyin: BAH-leh. ee WEH-boh see KOH-meh
steps.pt: 👂 'Right. And do you eat egg?' — one word back: sí, or no.
One label further out, and this one has no shorthand at all. You say the whole list, every time.

steps.es: Soy vegano: sin carne, sin pescado, sin huevo y sin leche.
steps.pinyin: soy beh-GAH-noh · seen KAR-neh, seen pehs-KAH-dhoh, seen WEH-boh ee seen LEH-cheh
steps.pt: I'm vegan: no meat, no fish, no egg and no milk.
steps.tts: Soy vegano: sin carne, sin pescado, sin huevo y sin leche.

steps.promptPt: Same table, and this time nothing that ever came off an animal — not the dairy either, and not the eggs. Give the kitchen the label and then the whole list. Speak now.
steps.es: Soy vegano: sin carne, sin pescado, sin huevo y sin leche.
steps.pinyin: soy beh-GAH-noh · seen KAR-neh, seen pehs-KAH-dhoh, seen WEH-boh ee seen LEH-cheh
steps.pt: the label, then the whole list

steps.es: Pues le hago una ensalada. Sin atún, claro.
steps.pinyin: pwehs leh AH-goh OO-nah en-sah-LAH-dhah. seen ah-TOON, KLAH-roh
steps.pt: 👂 'I'll do you a salad. Without tuna, obviously.' — obviously is doing a great deal of work in that sentence.
steps.tts: Pues le hago una ensalada. Sin atún, claro.

steps.pt: The label says who you are. Yesterday's two syllables take the thing straight back off the plate.

steps.promptPt: A station coffee counter, six people behind you, and the thing that goes into a cortado is the thing you cannot have. Head it off. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: seen LEH-cheh, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: without it
Rung two is not a frame. It is one sentence, welded shut. You say it whole or you do not say it.

steps.es: Es una alergia grave. Puedo acabar en el hospital.
steps.pinyin: es OO-nah ah-LEHR-khyah GRAH-beh · PWEH-dhoh ah-kah-BAR en el ohs-pee-TAL
steps.pt: It's a serious allergy. I could end up in hospital.
Eyes up, not down at the tablecloth. And there is the punch you warmed up with: os-pee-TAL.

steps.promptPt: He nodded and wrote nothing down, and he is halfway to the next table. Make it medical, out loud, and look at him while you do it. Speak now.
steps.es: Es una alergia grave. Puedo acabar en el hospital.
steps.pinyin: es OO-nah ah-LEHR-khyah GRAH-beh · PWEH-dhoh ah-kah-BAR en el ohs-pee-TAL
steps.pt: how bad it gets

steps.es: Bueno, un poquito seguro que no pasa nada.
steps.pinyin: BWEH-noh, oon poh-KEE-toh seh-GOO-roh keh noh PAH-sah NAH-dhah
steps.pt: 👂 'A little bit surely won't hurt.' — it is not defiance. It is the next rung, and you have it.
steps.tts: Bueno, un poquito seguro que no pasa nada.

steps.pt: And now the hammer. Five words that do more work than any other sentence in this course.

steps.pinyin: es ah-LEHR-khyah, noh es mah-NEE-ah
steps.pt: It's an allergy, not a fussy preference.
Manía is precisely what you are being suspected of: a fussy private rule. Naming it out loud kills it.

steps.promptPt: She is still smiling, and she has just told you that a tiny bit never hurt anybody. Answer that, in five words. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: es ah-LEHR-khyah, noh es mah-NEE-ah
steps.pt: the hammer

steps.pinyin: BAH-leh, BAH-leh. pehr-DOH-neh
steps.pt: 👂 'All right, all right. Sorry.' — the hammer lands, and nobody is offended.
Rung three moves it off the waiter altogether. He is not the person holding the pan.

steps.pinyin: PWEH-dheh ah-bee-SAR en koh-THEE-nah, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Could you tell the kitchen, please?

steps.promptPt: He has taken the order and he is already turning away. Stop him, and move it to the people at the stove. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: PWEH-dheh ah-bee-SAR en koh-THEE-nah, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: pass it through the door
Now the half nobody warns you about. Nothing here ambushes you with chilli. It ambushes you with pork.
In a kitchen that reaches for cured pork the way yours reaches for a stock cube, ham is seasoning.
Seasoning does not get read out with the dish. So the judías verdes — the green beans — come with cubes through them.
Which means the frame you want is not «is it vegetarian». It is one word: lleva. Does it carry.

steps.pinyin: YEH-bah khah-MOHN oh choh-REE-thoh
steps.pt: Does it have ham or chorizo in it?
Lleva stays put. What comes after it is the only thing that ever moves. Emilio, in Valencia.

steps.es: ¿Lleva caldo de pescado o de carne?
steps.pinyin: YEH-bah KAL-doh deh pehs-KAH-dhoh oh deh KAR-neh
steps.pt: Does it have fish or meat stock in it?

steps.promptPt: A taberna two streets off the square. The green beans are the safe-looking thing on the board and you are two seconds from ordering them. Ask first. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: YEH-bah khah-MOHN oh choh-REE-thoh
steps.pt: the cured pork, either kind

steps.promptPt: Valencia, and the rice with vegetables on it sounds perfect. What the pot was built on before the vegetables went in is not written anywhere. Ask. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Lleva caldo de pescado o de carne?
steps.pinyin: YEH-bah KAL-doh deh pehs-KAH-dhoh oh deh KAR-neh
steps.pt: what the pot was built on

steps.promptPt: A weekday lunch, and the sauce on the second course is thick. You cannot see what thickened it, and the word on the packet would not help either. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: YEH-bah ah-REE-nah oh GLOO-ten
steps.pt: the white powder, and the other word

steps.promptPt: A pastry counter on a Sunday morning, four trays under glass, and the one you want has something brown and chopped on top. Put the question to her. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: YEH-bah FROO-tohs SEH-kohs
steps.pt: almonds, hazelnuts, any of them
Asking is half of it. The other half is asking for a change, and these kitchens are readier than their reputation.
The frame is the one you opened today with. Whatever you want left out is the only part that moves.

steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-dheh ah-THEHR seen AH-khoh
steps.pt: Could you make it without garlic?

steps.promptPt: You want the dish, just not the garlic in it. Ask them to make it without. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-dheh ah-THEHR seen AH-khoh
steps.pt: Could you make it without garlic?

steps.promptPt: Different table, different plate. The lentils sound wonderful and there is cured pork diced all through them. Ask the kitchen to leave it out. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: meh loh PWEH-dheh ah-THEHR seen khah-MOHN
steps.pt: Could you make it without ham?

steps.es: Es que ya viene con el jamón dentro, cocinado.
steps.pinyin: es keh yah BYEH-neh kon el khah-MOHN DEN-troh, koh-thee-NAH-dhoh
steps.pt: 👂 'It comes with the ham cooked into it.' — that is a no, said helpfully. Order something else.
steps.tts: Es que ya viene con el jamón dentro, cocinado.

steps.pt: Now the question no phrasebook gives you, because it is not about an ingredient at all.
The croquettes, the squid, the chips and the fish go through the same oil. Chips are not neutral.

steps.es: ¿Lo fríen en la misma freidora que el pescado?
steps.pinyin: loh FREE-en en lah MEES-mah fray-DOH-rah keh el pehs-KAH-dhoh
steps.pt: Do you fry it in the same fryer as the fish?

steps.promptPt: You ordered chips because chips felt safe. There is one vat of oil behind that counter and everything on the board has been through it. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Lo fríen en la misma freidora que el pescado?
steps.pinyin: loh FREE-en en lah MEES-mah fray-DOH-rah keh el pehs-KAH-dhoh
steps.pt: the equipment, not the recipe
GUIRI ALERT. You are being careful. You are reading the label. You want to know about preservatives.
So you point at the chorizo and say: ¿lleva preservativos? You have just asked whether it contains condoms.
The word you wanted is conservantes. A Spanish word that looks exactly like yours is a trap with good marketing.

steps.pinyin: YEH-bah kon-sehr-BAHN-tehs
steps.pt: Does it contain preservatives? (the word you actually wanted)
Watch what happens on the night you speak well. She compliments your accent — and the plate still has ham through it.
The compliment was real. It only means she heard a chatty tourist, not a person with a medical problem.
So: the five words, straight face, eyes up. And the card on the table. Both of them, not one or the other.
Not at a counter three deep at midnight, mind. Nobody there is talking to anybody. Card out first, no sentences.
And here is what you never have to do. You never explain why, and you never apologise for asking.
Olive oil is not a battle worth having. It is what the whole country fries in and it is very good.
Garlic is not one either, unless it genuinely hurts you. Ask once, when you order, then eat your dinner.
Now the safest thing you own, and it is not your accent. It is a piece of card in your pocket.
SOY ALÉRGICO A, then your list, then PUEDE SER GRAVE. Reception will write it, or print it before you fly.
Show it, do not perform it. Photograph it too — the paper one always ends up in the other jacket.
There is a second card, and that one is theirs. Anywhere serving food that did not come sealed holds an allergen list.
Ask for it and this stops being a chat about your pronunciation. It becomes something they have to answer.

steps.pinyin: TYEH-nen lah KAR-tah deh ah-LEHR-kheh-nohs
steps.pt: Do you have the allergen list?

steps.promptPt: You have explained twice and you are still not sure it landed. Stop explaining and ask for the document instead. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: TYEH-nen lah KAR-tah deh ah-LEHR-kheh-nohs
steps.pt: the paper, not the conversation
Whole ladder in one scene. Carmen is the waitress, Emilio is you. Listen to how fast it ends.

steps.pinyin: keh bahn ah toh-MAR
steps.pt: — What are you having? (the waitress)

steps.pinyin: soy ah-LEHR-khee-koh ah lohs FROO-tohs SEH-kohs
steps.pt: — I'm allergic to nuts.

steps.es: Vale, un poquito no pasa nada, ¿no?
steps.pinyin: BAH-leh, oon poh-KEE-toh noh PAH-sah NAH-dhah, noh
steps.pt: — Right, a tiny bit's fine though, isn't it?

steps.es: No. Es alergia, no es manía. Es una alergia grave.

steps.pt: — No. It's an allergy, not a fad. It's a serious allergy.

steps.pt: — Of course. I'll bring you the allergen list.
One more scene, three tables away, and it is the green beans. Same two people. Listen to where it lands.

steps.pt: — The green beans are very good today. (the waitress)

steps.pinyin: YEH-bah khah-MOHN oh choh-REE-thoh
steps.pt: — Does it have ham or chorizo in it?

steps.pinyin: see, YEH-bah oon POH-koh deh khah-MOHN · PEH-roh mwee poh-KEE-toh
steps.pt: — Yes, it's got a bit of ham. But only a tiny bit.
steps.tts: Sí, lleva un poco de jamón. Pero muy poquito.

steps.es: Claro que sí. ¿Y el arroz? Ese lleva caldo de pescado.

steps.pt: — Then no, thank you. What do you recommend?
She volunteered the fish stock. She only did that because he had already asked one ugly question out loud.
Count the rooms. A taberna, a rice pot in Valencia, a weekday lunch, a pastry counter. Four, one word.
Nobody gave you those four questions. You built them out of one word you already own.
You will hand a Spanish kitchen something it can act on. Most people who spend a fortnight here order and hope.
Shadowing. Out loud, with them, every syllable paid in full. These two travel further than the rest.

steps.pinyin: es ah-LEHR-khyah, noh es mah-NEE-ah
steps.pt: It's an allergy, not a fussy preference.

steps.pinyin: YEH-bah khah-MOHN oh choh-REE-thoh
steps.pt: Does it have ham or chorizo in it?
One more out loud and you are done. A counter we have not stood at yet.

steps.promptPt: A market stall, a tray of cooked red peppers, and the thing that goes into every pan in this country would genuinely hurt you. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: YEH-bah AH-khoh
steps.pt: the one that is in everything
That is it. Three rungs, one word, and a card that works when the room is too loud for any of it. Hasta luego.

aprofundar.titulo: The card, the ending on your own name, and where the food hides things (optional reading)

secoes.corpo: Speech is the weakest link in a loud bar: your pronunciation, plus their hearing, plus a room at full volume. A printed card removes all three, and it is the reason this part exists at all — where the stakes are highest we hand you the safest artefact rather than the cleverest sentence. Ask reception to write it, or carry your own: SOY ALÉRGICO/A A: … PUEDE SER GRAVE. Show it, do not perform it. Keep a photograph of it on your phone as well, because the paper one always ends up in the other jacket. In the kit, the same card lives behind the 🃏 button, so it is two taps away with the phone locked.

exemplos.es: SOY ALÉRGICO A LOS FRUTOS SECOS. PUEDE SER GRAVE.
exemplos.pt: I am allergic to nuts. It can be serious. — the card, word for word

exemplos.es: ¿Se lo puede enseñar al cocinero, por favor?
exemplos.pt: seh loh PWEH-dheh en-seh-NYAR al koh-thee-NEH-roh — Could you show this to the chef, please?

secoes.titulo: The one place gender actually matters
secoes.corpo: Spanish gender is the most forgiving mistake in the language — say 'la problema' and your beer still arrives. There is exactly one place we do not let you relax, and it is here: the adjectives that describe YOU. A man is alérgico, celíaco, vegetariano, vegano; a woman is alérgica, celíaca, vegetariana, vegana. It matters not because it is grammar but because this is the sentence in which you are asking somebody to keep you out of hospital, and a clean, confident sentence is believed. The app already set your ending from your onboarding answer, and you will hear it used consistently from here on. You never choose it in the moment.

exemplos.pt: soy ah-LEHR-khee-kah al mah-REES-koh — woman speaking
soy ah-LEHR-khee-koh al mah-REES-koh — man speaking

secoes.titulo: Why the allergen list has to exist
secoes.corpo: EU Regulation 1169/2011, brought into Spanish law by Royal Decree 126/2015, obliges anyone serving food that did not arrive in a sealed packet — restaurants, bars, bakeries, market stalls — to hold allergen information for every dish and to make it available to you. It can be a folder, a laminated sheet, a screen or a spoken answer from trained staff, but it has to be there and it has to be accurate. That is why «¿Tienen la carta de alérgenos?» outranks every clever sentence you could build: it stops being a conversation about a foreigner's Spanish and becomes a request they are required to answer. If a place bristles at the question, you have learned something useful about that kitchen for free. (Source: AESAN, Reg. (UE) 1169/2011 and RD 126/2015. Worth re-checking before 2028.)

exemplos.pt: TYEH-nen lah KAR-tah deh ah-LEHR-kheh-nohs — Do you have the allergen list?

exemplos.es: ¿Me lo puede confirmar con la cocina?
exemplos.pt: meh loh PWEH-dheh kon-feer-MAR kon lah koh-THEE-nah — Can you confirm that with the kitchen?

secoes.titulo: The hiding places, ranked by how often they catch people
secoes.corpo: 1. Ham and chorizo as seasoning: judías verdes, espinacas, lentejas, sopa de verduras, and most things described as 'de la abuela'. 2. Stock: arroces and paellas 'de verduras' built on fish or meat caldo. 3. The shared fryer: croquetas, calamares, patatas and pescado through one vat of oil. 4. Hidden gluten: croquetas, anything rebozado (battered), flour-thickened sauces, and beer. 5. Fish where you did not look: anchoa in tinned things and in sauces, atún as standard in ensaladilla rusa, and salsa marinera, which is shellfish. None of this is deception. It is a kitchen where pork and stock do the job that salt and a stock cube do at home.

exemplos.pt: lah en-sah-lah-DEE-yah YEH-bah ah-TOON — Does the potato salad have tuna in it?
YEH-bah LEH-cheh — Does it have milk in it? (same word, new ingredient)

secoes.titulo: «Vegetal» is a description, not a promise
secoes.corpo: The word on the menu describes the visible contents, not the recipe. Crema de verduras is frequently built on chicken stock and finished with jamón; a menu section headed VERDURAS means the vegetable is the star, not that no animal was involved. Fish is the sharpest edge of this: in ordinary Spanish usage carne means meat from land animals, so «no como carne» does not exclude anchovies, tuna or prawns, and a waiter who brings you fish after that sentence is not being careless. Say «ni pescado» every single time. The clean, unambiguous words are vegetariano/a and vegano/a — and vegano is well understood in cities, less so in small inland towns, where the full list (sin carne, sin pescado, sin huevo, sin leche) does the work instead.

exemplos.es: Soy vegetariana: no como carne ni pescado.
exemplos.pt: soy beh-kheh-tah-RYAH-nah, noh KOH-moh KAR-neh nee pehs-KAH-dhoh
TYEH-nen AHL-goh beh-GAH-noh — Do you have anything vegan?

secoes.titulo: Cross-contamination, and what is actually reasonable to ask
secoes.corpo: The shared fryer is real and worth asking about if your allergy is severe: «¿Lo fríen en la misma freidora que el pescado?» Same logic for the plancha, the grill: «¿Lo hacen en la misma plancha?» What is NOT worth asking about is olive oil — it is the cooking medium of the entire country, it is excellent, and asking for your food to be cooked in something else marks you as the difficult table for no benefit at all. Pick your battles: fryer yes, oil no. And note the shape of rung three — «¿Puede avisar en cocina?» — which is the same frame you already use for «¿me puede escribir?» and «¿me puede recomendar algo para…?». One frame, three completely different emergencies.

exemplos.es: ¿Lo hacen en la misma plancha que el pescado?
exemplos.pt: loh AH-then en lah MEES-mah PLAHN-chah keh el pehs-KAH-dhoh — Same grill as the fish?

exemplos.es: ¿Puede usar una sartén limpia, por favor?
exemplos.pt: PWEH-dheh oo-SAR OO-nah sar-TEN LEEM-pyah — Could you use a clean pan, please?

secoes.titulo: False friends that live in this exact conversation
secoes.corpo: preservativo = condom (preservatives are conservantes). excitado = sexually aroused (excited is emocionado, or tengo muchas ganas). constipado = having a cold, NOT constipated (that is estreñido — and you will need this one at the pharmacy, not the restaurant). molestar is a perfectly polite word meaning 'to bother', so do not avoid it. And en absoluto does not mean 'absolutely': it means 'absolutely not', so if the waiter asks whether you enjoyed it, en absoluto is a very cold thing to say by accident. Use ¡totalmente! or ¡desde luego!

exemplos.pt: YEH-bah kon-sehr-BAHN-tehs — Does it contain preservatives?

exemplos.es: Estoy muy emocionado con el viaje.
exemplos.pt: ehs-TOY mwee eh-moh-thyoh-NAH-dhoh kon el BYAH-kheh — I'm very excited about the trip.
